clue.text: Game, this riotous nonsense breaking free in toilet

indicators.note: the word in tells us everything before it sits inside the lavatory word

parts.note: bog is ... slang for a toilet

indicators.note: breaking means splitting open the word for free so other letters go inside it

parts.note: to free something of a nuisance is to rid it

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters of this are thrown into a new order

parts.note: bull is slang for nonsense, short for a coarser word

explanation.surface: Someone is ranting about a game, its riotous nonsense breaking out in a lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riotous' scrambles this, the result plus BULL is put inside RID by 'breaking', and 'in' sets that in BOG. The game is a rough British playground chase where runners try to get past catchers.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a rough playground chasing game played in British schools, where runners try to cross past catchers.

clue.text: Paramount directed, for Spooner, a film

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words have their first letters exchanged

parts.note: paramount means main, chief
directed, as of a business, means ran

explanation.surface: A Paramount film directed in the voice of the famously muddled Reverend Spooner.
explanation.walkthrough: Paramount looks like the film studio, and a film is the answer, which helps the misdirection: here it just means MAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1988 Hollywood picture starred Dustin Hoffman and Tom Cruise, so it is an example of a film.

clue.text: Cut stolen by Tory, regularly — he'll take the money

indicators.note: something stolen by a thief is held inside, so these letters go inside the others
regularly means taking every other letter of the word Tory

parts.note: to axe is to cut, as in cutting jobs or spending

explanation.surface: A Tory cut that he regularly steals; he is the one who takes the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes T and R from Tory, and 'stolen by' puts AXE between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who levies taxes collects money from people, so he takes the money.

clue.text: Inner area of plant identified retaining power, (zero) before party turning up

indicators.note: retaining means holding on to, so the power letter is held inside the word for identified

parts.note: to have identified something is to have seen or spotted it, so saw
P is the standard abbreviation for power in physics
zero resembles the letter O

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the party word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a do is an informal word for a party

explanation.surface: A botanical description identifying an inner part of a plant, with an odd aside about power and a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reads the party word from the bottom up in this down clue. The bracketed zero is the letter O; 'before' just places it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the soft living wood of a tree trunk, lying between the bark and the heartwood, carrying the sap.

clue.text: See 1
Not bright to ignore capital, making saving

indicators.note: capital here is the first letter, which is dropped from the word for not bright

parts.note: a sunless day is dull, not bright

explanation.surface: A dull outlook that ignores the capital city, making savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving' is the old preposition meaning except, as in 'saving your presence', not putting money aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean except or but for: 'saving that' and the conditional conjunction work alike.

clue.text: This contemplated surfacing to bandage hit, a rabid sea monster

indicators.note: to bandage something is to wrap round it, so the reversed letters enclose the others
in a down clue surfacing means coming up, so the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: people are said to contemplate their navel when lost in self-absorbed thought

indicators.note: rabid means wild and frenzied, so the letters of hit and a are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rabid sea monster that someone contemplated as it surfaced, with a bandage for a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Navel-gazing is the idea behind 'This contemplated'. 'surfacing' turns that word upwards to LEVAN, and 'to bandage' wraps it round the letters 'rabid' makes from hit and a.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the vast biblical sea creature named in Job and the Psalms, now used for any huge monster.

clue.text: Monarch, abandoning sinking boat at sea, comes by

indicators.note: at sea means confused or adrift, so the remaining letters are jumbled
abandoning means leaving behind, so the monarch word is removed from sinking

parts.note: a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A monarch abandons a sinking boat at sea and happens upon something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoning' takes KING from sinking, leaving SIN, and 'at sea' rearranges SIN plus BOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To come by something is to get hold of it, a plain synonym for acquiring.

clue.text: Don't stop till you've finished — try trotters and all?

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt
a pig entire, trotters included, is the complete animal, a whole porker

explanation.surface: Advice to see a job through, followed by a suggestion to eat the pig, feet included.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the playful reading of the idiom: a hog with its trotters is the entire pig.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to do something thoroughly and completely, holding nothing back.

clue.text: Game, Jack in this number?

parts.note: J is the abbreviation for jack in a pack of cards
this clue is number ten, and X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A card player asks whether the jack is in this number of the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'this number' refers to the clue's own number, 10, written as Roman X.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a children's game: when two people say the same thing at once, one calls it out first.

clue.text: Bent clip, ivory, moulded round first of teeth

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the single letter
moulded means shaped anew, so the letters of clip and ivory are rearranged
first of means the opening letter of teeth is used

explanation.surface: A bent clip and some ivory moulded around a tooth, like dental work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bent' looks like an adjective describing the clip, but it is the noun meaning an inclination.
explanation.definitionFit: A bent is a natural inclination or tendency, the same as a leaning towards something.

clue.text: Germ doctor tracks in videoing heart

indicators.note: the word in places the doctor and tracks inside the central letters
heart means the middle letters of videoing are taken

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
RY is an abbreviation for railway, the tracks

explanation.surface: A doctor who studies germs tracks them by videoing a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Germ' suggests a doctor's microbe; here it means the first stage of life. 'heart' takes the central pair of letters of videoing.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ in the sense of a seed or bud is the earliest stage of a developing organism.

clue.text: Spanish in contrast to her serenity?

parts.note: his is the masculine possessive, the opposite of her
panic is the opposite of serenity; 'in contrast to' applies to this word too

explanation.surface: A question contrasting a man's serenity with a woman's.
explanation.walkthrough: Both pieces are opposites: 'in contrast to' governs her and serenity alike.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means relating to Spain or Spanish-speaking peoples, so it fits Spanish.

clue.text: Game to have a go at, blue then red

parts.note: to knock someone is to criticise or have a go at them
blue means sad, and so does down
ginger is a reddish hair colour

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to try a game, feeling blue and then going red.
explanation.walkthrough: The game is a British children's prank of knocking on a door and running away before it is answered.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a children's prank game of knocking on doors and running off before anyone comes.

clue.text: Solver primarily in support of clues, not foreign legion

indicators.note: in a down clue a support goes underneath, so the solver letter goes at the bottom
foreign means strange or alien, so the letters of clues and not are rearranged
primarily means the first letter of solver

explanation.surface: A solver has supported clues, as long as no foreign legion is involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign legion' is the false phrase: legion is the definition, an adjective meaning numerous. In a down clue the support sits at the bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Legion used as an adjective means very numerous, too many to number.

clue.text: See 27
General having fit behind Churchillian salute

indicators.note: behind means the fit word comes after the salute letter

parts.note: Winston Churchill's famous gesture was the V for victory sign
an ague is a fit of shivering fever

explanation.surface: A general suffers a fit just after giving Churchill's victory salute.
explanation.walkthrough: General looks like an army officer, but it is the adjective meaning broad or imprecise.
explanation.definitionFit: A general description is broad and imprecise, lacking definite detail.

clue.text: A rival to us concealing one's disbelief

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so the letters for one's go into the rival word

parts.note: 'them' as opposed to 'us' names the other side, the rivals
one is I and the 's is read as is, giving I'S

explanation.surface: A rival to our side hides his lack of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'us and them' idiom supplies the rivals: the other side is them.
explanation.definitionFit: This is disbelief in the existence of any god, a rejection of religious faith.

clue.text: Broad agreement on sloppy leadership in survey

indicators.note: the word in tells us these letters are placed within the survey word

parts.note: a census is an official survey of a population

indicators.note: leadership means the leading letter of sloppy

explanation.surface: Broad agreement that the leadership was sloppy, according to a survey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leadership' gives the first letter of sloppy, and 'in' places it, with on, inside the survey word.
explanation.definitionFit: General agreement among a group, when nearly everyone holds the same view, is the sense here.

clue.text: Italian chap claiming fine to accept the delivery

indicators.note: claiming means taking in and holding, so the fine letter goes inside

parts.note: signor is the Italian title for a man, like Mister
F stands for fine, as on pencil leads

explanation.surface: An Italian man claims a fine before accepting a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: The fine letter splits the Italian title into two words, sign and for.
explanation.definitionFit: To put your signature to a receipt for a parcel is to acknowledge you have received it.

clue.text: Spoon perhaps required, as classy figure is raised on lager, initially

parts.note: U means upper-class, a classic usage from the 1950s debate about U and non-U
ten is a figure, a number

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards
initially means the first letter of lager

explanation.surface: A spoon is needed, as a posh person raises a number on a lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns IS to SI; in a down clue 'on' puts these pieces above L.
explanation.definitionFit: A spoon is one example of a kitchen or dining implement, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Go without watch — about five?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the stare word goes round the five letter

parts.note: to stare is to watch fixedly
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone forgoes a watch, asking if it is about five o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'watch' looks like a timepiece, matching the time question; it is the verb, STARE.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without food for a long time is to be deprived of nourishment, starving.

clue.text: Game with two hammers felt frantic

indicators.note: frantic means wild and agitated, so the letters before it are thoroughly rearranged

explanation.surface: Playing a game with two hammers, someone felt frantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' looks like a link but its letters are part of the anagram, which uses all eighteen letters of WITH TWO HAMMERS FELT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a children's playground game in which players creep up on a 'wolf' who calls out times.

clue.text: See 14
Defenceless clergyman upholding Mozart's character?

annotationWithheld.why: Defenceless clergyman upholding Mozart's character? (5): DEAN holding K, read upwards, gives NAKED, but the single word 'upholding' is both the container and the reversal indicator

clue.text: See 23
Game — not entirely important around one's school, as following

indicators.note: around means the shortened word surrounds the following letters
not entirely means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: key means important, as in a key factor
one is I and the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A game that is not wholly important around one's school, as follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims the last letter off the word for important; 'following' only says the second word of the answer follows the first.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a playground game where children chase one another and kiss whoever they catch.

clue.text: Dazzling charmer, big hitter?

definitions.meaning: an attractive, stunning person is informally a real knockout
someone who strikes things hard, such as a powerful tennis player hitting overheads

explanation.surface: A description of a dazzling, charming person who may also hit hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means a very attractive person, and literally one who breaks things with blows.

clue.text: Is it just for cooking pancakes? Good question

definitions.text: Is it just for cooking pancakes?

parts.note: a riddle is a puzzling question

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a pan is only for pancakes, and is told it is a good question.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question whose answer is the flat iron plate used for pancakes.
explanation.definitionFit: This flat iron cooking plate is used for pancakes, drop scones and similar foods.
